reviews.note: NBC reviewed the Legion Go 2 but the article URL/score could not be resolved this session (ID-guessing 404s); recorded as null per schema rule 5.

reviews.outlet: Engadget (2026 Steam Deck re-check, mentions Legion Go 2)
reviews.quote: competitors (Xbox Ally/Ally X, Legion Go 2) beat it in raw Time Spy, but in real-world applications, Valve's handheld often comes out on top

praises: 8.8" 2560x1600 144Hz OLED is the best display in any shipping handheld — big, per-pixel blacks, and 144Hz in lighter titles feels console-smooth
Detachable Legion TrueStrike controllers with hall-effect sticks, a 3ms low-latency polling mode and rear mappable buttons feel like a proper controller rather than a bolted-on compromise
74.25Wh battery plus Zen 5 efficiency gives genuinely usable handheld runtime — a big step over the 2023 Legion Go, enough for long flights at low TDP
Two full-speed USB4 ports and a UHS-II microSD slot make external SSDs, docks and storage expansion painless (unlike the Deck's single USB-C + UHS-I)
Full Windows 11 + 32GB RAM means Game Pass, anti-cheat multiplayer and any launcher work — the SteamOS gap that blocks the Deck simply does not exist here
complaints: ~982g with controllers attached is the heaviest mainstream handheld; arms tire in handheld mode and the tablet-to-controller dock joint feels less rigid than an integrated chassis
Glossy OLED at ~500 nits SDR with no anti-glare/etched option: outdoor and bright-room readability is clearly worse than the etched-glass Steam Deck OLED 1TB
Windows-on-a-handheld rough edges remain: wake-from-sleep bugs, Legion Space/launcher friction and driver updates — nothing like SteamOS instant resume
Right-side coil whine and an audible fan under sustained 15W+ load, loudest when docked and charging
Soldered RAM and no webcam: video calls or streaming need an external camera, and there is no RAM upgrade path at all

standouts: Largest and fastest display of any mainstream handheld (8.8" 144Hz OLED)
Best raw handheld GPU performance in its class (Radeon 820M, 16 CU) — beats Deck and Xbox Ally X in Time Spy
Detachable controllers + 2x USB4 + UHS-II make it the most desktop-adaptable handheld
dealbreakers: No webcam at all, and Windows handheld ergonomics (wake/sleep, no instant resume) still trail SteamOS
Nearly 1kg in the hands — the worst in-hand portability of the handheld group
design_philosophy: Lenovo's thesis is that the handheld should be a full Windows PC first and a console second: a tablet big enough to be the whole device, with controllers that detach so the same hardware becomes a small laptop, a docked mini-PC, or a plain tablet. This 32GB/1TB tier is the flagship of that idea — the RAM and storage headroom that makes the Windows-desktop half of the pitch real (multitasking, emulation, larger game libraries) rather than a compromise, at the cost of being the heaviest and most expensive handheld in the group.
